Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let
$A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. A matrix $B\in M_{n\times m}(\mathbb F)$ is a
**Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse** of $A$ when

$$ABA=A,\qquad BAB=B,$$

and the two square products are self-adjoint:

$$ (AB)^*=AB,\qquad (BA)^*=BA. $$

When such a matrix exists and is unique, it is denoted by $A^+$.

The four displayed relations are the **Penrose equations**. They are written in
the matrix product and adjoint conventions of
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]] and
[[thm-matrix-of-the-adjoint-is-the-conjugate-transpose]].

For every matrix $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$ over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or
$\mathbb C$, there exists a unique matrix $A^+\in M_{n\times m}(\mathbb F)$
satisfying the four Penrose equations of
[[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]].

derivations.claim: The block matrix of $H_A$ is $\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\A^*&0\end{pmatrix}$. Its adjoint, by [F2], is the same block matrix, so $H_A^*=H_A$.

Multiplying the SVD in [F1] gives $Av_j=\sigma_j u_j$ and $A^*u_j=\sigma_jv_j$. Therefore $H_A(u_j,v_j)=\sigma_j(u_j,v_j)$ and $H_A(u_j,-v_j)=-\sigma_j(u_j,-v_j)$. After division by $\sqrt2$ these are unit eigenvectors. Orthonormality of the singular pairs makes all such vectors mutually orthogonal.

In the SVD bases, write $A=U\Sigma V^*$ with positive diagonal entries $\sigma_j$. The diagonal matrix $\Sigma^+$ that replaces each positive entry by $1/\sigma_j$ and leaves zero entries zero satisfies $\Sigma\Sigma^+\Sigma=\Sigma$, $\Sigma^+\Sigma\Sigma^+=\Sigma^+$, and both products $\Sigma\Sigma^+$ and $\Sigma^+\Sigma$ are diagonal projections. Unitary transport shows $V\Sigma^+U^*$ satisfies the four equations in [F3], so uniqueness gives $A^+=V\Sigma^+U^*$ and $A^+u_j=v_j/\sigma_j$.

The equation $H_A(x,y)=0$ is equivalent to $Ay=0$ and $A^*x=0$, so $\ker H_A=\ker(A^*)\oplus\ker(A)$. Together with step 1.2, the nonzero eigenvalue magnitudes are exactly the positive singular values, each appearing with both signs. Thus when there is positive rank their maximum-to-minimum ratio is unchanged.

The vectors from step 1.2 together with orthonormal bases of $\ker(A^*)$ and $\ker(A)$ form an orthonormal eigenbasis of the direct sum. Define $G$ on this basis by $Gw_{j,+}=w_{j,+}/\sigma_j$, $Gw_{j,-}=-w_{j,-}/\sigma_j$, and $G=0$ on the kernel. Then $H_AG$ and $GH_A$ are self-adjoint projections, while diagonal multiplication gives $H_AGH_A=H_A$ and $GH_AG=G$. Thus $G$ satisfies [F3], and uniqueness gives $G=H_A^+$. Since $(u_j,0)=(w_{j,+}+w_{j,-})/\sqrt2$, this definition gives $H_A^+(u_j,0)=(0,v_j/\sigma_j)$. Complete the positive left singular vectors to the left singular basis from [F1]. The remaining basis vectors have zero singular coordinates, so the diagonal SVD gives $A^*u_j=0$ for each; hence they span the complementary part $\ker(A^*)$. Thus every $b\in\mathbb C^m$ has a decomposition $b=\sum_{j:\sigma_j>0}\beta_j u_j+b_0$ with $b_0\in\ker(A^*)$. Since $A^*b_0=0$, its positive left-singular coordinates vanish, so $\Sigma^+U^*b_0=0$ and the formula in step 1.3 gives $A^+b_0=0$. By step 2.1 $(b_0,0)\in\ker(H_A)$, so $H_A^+(b_0,0)=G(b_0,0)=0$. Applying the positive-pair calculation to the other summands gives $H_A^+(b,0)=(0,A^+b)$ for arbitrary $b$, including $b\notin\operatorname{ran}(A)$.

Write $\Delta=|\widetilde\lambda-\lambda|=|\delta|/t_0$. $$|x\rangle:=\frac{A^+b}{\|A^+b\|}\in\mathbb C^n,$$

Expand $|b\rangle=\sum_j\beta_j|u_j\rangle$ in [F1], with $\sum_j|\beta_j|^2=1$. Apply the supplied $B$ (or $B_A$ for a rectangular system) to prepare the input and its fixed work state, set $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, choose the least power of two $T\ge8(t_0+1)$ by certified comparisons, and let $L=\log_2T$. Initialize the phase register to $|0^L\rangle$ in big-endian order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$. This carrier chooses OP5's explicit table variant for preparing [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]]. Build the complete binary prefix tree on the $T$ leaves. At each level $\ell=0,\ldots,L-1$ and for each interval node $[a,b)$ at that level, put $m=(a+b)/2$ and compute the child masses $W_T(a,m)$ and $W_T(m,b)$ from the formula in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Store $r=W_T(a,m)/W_T(a,b)$ and apply $R_y(2\arcsin\sqrt r)$ to wire $q_{L-1-\ell}$, controlled on the preceding $\ell$ wires matching the path to $[a,b)$; encode bit $1$ as the left child and bit $0$ as the right child. Each nonempty mass is at least $T^{-2}$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Use certified interval arithmetic with absolute mass error at most $\epsilon_\Psi^2/(10^6L^2T^4)$; refine until each stored angle and its finite gate synthesis together give controlled-rotation operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi/(100T)$. The table contains $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations. Charge its one-time construction/data cost $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ and each forward/inverse preparation cost $C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ from [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]], including reversible lookup, control and finite gate synthesis. 2. In either the original full-space or alternative clean-workspace simulation mode, initialize all simulator work in zero and retain it coherently. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, set $t_j=2^jt_0/T$ and allocate $\eta_j=\epsilon/(8192\kappa L)$ to both its forward controlled call $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ and its reverse call. Apply $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ to the system controlled on wire $q_j$ being $1$, and act as identity on its $0$ branch. In the declared order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$, a phase label $\tau$ has bits $x_j$ with $\tau=\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}2^jx_j$, so the ideal controlled list applies $e^{+iH\tau t_0/T}$. Apply the negative-sign QFT, decode $y$ to signed $k=y$ for $y<T/2$ and $k=y-T$ otherwise, and set $\widetilde\lambda=2\pi k/t_0$. The total forward evolution time is $\sum_{j<L}t_j=t_0(1-1/T)<t_0$, and the sum of the $2L$ simulation error allocations is $\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. This uses the signed convention in [[lem-qa-26-phase-to-eigenvalue-unwrapping]].

3. Reversibly compute the flag angles and sign from $\widetilde\lambda$ using [[def-qa-26-hhl-reciprocal-filter]]. Write $p=|f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|$, $r=\sqrt{1-p^2}$, $\alpha=2\arcsin p$, and $\beta=2\arcsin(g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)/r)$. These are defined at every decoded grid point because [[lem-qa-26-hhl-filter-geometry]] gives $p\le1/2$, $0\le g\le1/2$, and $r\ge\sqrt3/2$, so $g/r\le1/\sqrt3<1$. First apply $R_y(\alpha)$ to $q_0$ conditioned on $q_1=0$, acting as identity on the $q_1=1$ subspace. Next apply $R_y(\beta)$ to $q_1$ conditioned on $q_0=0$, acting as identity on the $q_0=1$ subspace. All three factors fix the unused label $|11\rangle$. 4. Reverse the QFT, every actual controlled simulation circuit, and sine preparation, retaining the flag and all simulator work. This gives a unitary flagged preparation $V$ and its exact circuit inverse $V^\dagger$. Let $\Pi_{\rm good}$ be the well-flag projection in Hermitian mode and the product of the well-flag projection and tagged domain projection in rectangular mode; these two projections act on distinct registers and commute. Let $p=\|\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle\|^2$. Apply the finite capped amplification procedure proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-capped-amplification]] with success projection $\Pi_{\rm good}$, lower bound $p_{\mathrm{low}}=1/(16\kappa^2)$ and failure target $\rho$. Its success reflection and verification test both the well flag and the domain tag in rectangular mode; charge their actual costs to $C_{\rm ref}$ and $C_{\rm ver}$. The circuit uses no uniform-register phase-tail estimate: its phase distribution is the sine-window kernel proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-kernel-moment]]. Its $G_\Psi,C_\Psi,C_{\rm sim},C_{\rm QFT}^{+/-},C_{\rm flag}$, reflection, verification and $B/B^\dagger$ costs remain separate inputs.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

citations.quote: Let $H$ have the exact sorted $d$-sparse Hermitian XOR-location/value interface of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], with $N,d\ge1$. An optional support-list variant is also admissible: each row lists at most $d$ distinct columns in strictly increasing order, contains every nonzero column exactly once, and may additionally list zero-valued columns. Its row and column support lists agree under transposition; in the Hermitian case the row list at $j$ supplies the column list at $j$. The total XOR value oracle gives the exact decoded matrix, including any listed zeros. Missing slots use the same distinguished sentinel. No zero test on the matrix values is needed to form a supplied support union. An approximation to a different target matrix requires a separate operator-error bound. Put $M=2^{\lceil\log_2(N+d)\rceil}$ and $\widetilde H=H\oplus0$ on the $M$-label register. Given a positive certified bound $h\ge\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$, an exact costed preparation $d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|l\rangle$, and costed exact value-decoding and flag-rotation arithmetic, one can construct a unitary whose clean block is $\widetilde H/(dh)$. It and its actual adjoint and coherent controlled versions use $O(\log(d+1))$ QA20 location calls and $O(1)$ value calls each. Index bits, reversible workspace, search arithmetic, comparisons, uniform preparation, flags and gate precision remain separately charged. In particular $h=1$ is admissible when $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le1$, without computing the global maximum entry. The stronger separately supplied in-place-location interface keeps its original constant location-call count.

Let $\tau=\alpha|t|$ and $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)$, with $0<\epsilon<1$. In the nontrivial branch $\tau>\epsilon$, put $S=\tau+L/\ln(e+L/\tau)$. The small-time-aware simulator of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]] uses zero signal queries when $\tau\le\epsilon$. When $\tau>\epsilon$, the OP4 degree satisfies $d=O(S)$. The complete OAA circuit uses at most $3(d_E+d_O)\le6d$ ordinary $U/U^*$ signal calls, where $d_E,d_O\le d$ are the even and odd QSP degrees. It uses $3(d_E+d_O+2)$ projector-phase slots and therefore $6(d_E+d_O+2)$ controlled-reflection calls, by [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. Coherent selection of each real sequence against identity uses exactly one controlled signal call when that sequence degree is odd and none when it is even; because the selection occurs in each of the three OAA blocks $W,W^*,W$, the total is $3(\mathbf1_{d_E\text{ odd}}+\mathbf1_{d_O\text{ odd}})\le6$ controlled signal calls. The $\Phi/-\Phi$ branch itself controls phases, not signal calls. Any external control of the complete simulator controls and charges the whole block.

Gate, depth, width, ancilla, classical bit, precision, PREPARE/SELECT, phase-list-generation, and sparse-location/value costs remain separate coordinates. For a $d_H$-row-sparse input with supplied-permutation bound $h\ge h_{\max}$, the $h=0$ branch encodes $H=0$ with normalization $1$ and uses no location or value calls. If $h>0$, [[thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding-correctness]] gives normalization $\alpha=d_Hh$; choosing the tight bound $h=h_{\max}$ gives $\alpha=d_Hh_{\max}$. Multiply the signal-query count by the actual supplied sparse-encoding cost, including any location-permutation completion. The optional sorted-XOR mode has the same normalization $d_Hh$ for a supplied positive entry bound $h$ and multiplies the signal count by $O(\log(d_H+1))$ location calls and $O(1)$ value calls per signal, including inverses and coherent controls. No cost-free conversion from XOR row-location access is claimed. If $\tau$ is bounded above and below by positive constants as $\epsilon\to0$, the query bound specializes to $O(\tau+L/\ln L)=O(\tau+\ln(1/\epsilon)/\ln\ln(1/\epsilon))$. This is an upper bound; no matching lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access or for the additive precision term is asserted.

For every promised input of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]], a successful output satisfies the clean-input isometry error bound $\|V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$. It also satisfies the corresponding reference-system trace-distance bound after tracing the work registers.

Let $J:H\to K$ be an isometry of nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, $V$ a unitary on $H$, and $U$ a unitary on $K$. If $\|UJ-JV\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$, then $\|U^*J-JV^*\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$. The same inequalities hold after adjoining an arbitrary finite reference space or coherently controlling $U$ and $V$ against identity.

More generally, let $U_1,\ldots,U_s$ be actual unitaries on $K$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_s$ ideal unitaries on $H$, with $\|U_jJ-JV_j\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j$. Then

The empty products give zero error. Each bound concerns the clean input subspace $\operatorname{ran}J$; none assumes that an actual intermediate state belongs to that subspace or claims a full-space approximation on arbitrary dirty-work inputs.

Input a self-adjoint $H$ with $\|H\|\le1$, a unit input state $|b\rangle$ supported only on eigenvalues satisfying $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, and a supplied finite exact representation of the cutoff $\kappa\ge1$ that supports certified arithmetic and rational comparisons. Supply costed $B,B^\dagger$ and controlled/inverse simulation access as in [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]]. The accuracy and failure inputs are exact rational values $\epsilon=p_\epsilon/q_\epsilon$ and $\rho=p_\rho/q_\rho$, with positive binary-encoded integers and $0<p_\epsilon\le q_\epsilon$, $0<p_\rho<q_\rho$. Rectangular systems $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ use [[lem-qa-26-hermitian-dilation]]: choose a supplied rational scale $\Lambda\ge\|H_A\|$, use $H=H_A/\Lambda$, and set $\kappa=\Lambda/\gamma$ from the QLSP support gap $\gamma$. The QLSP definition supplies $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$ whenever the left singular coefficient of $b$ is nonzero; the dilation eigenvalues on this input support are $\pm\sigma_j/\Lambda$, so $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$. On $(\mathbb C^m\otimes W)\oplus(\mathbb C^n\otimes W)$ prepare the normalized codomain-supported input $(b/\|b\|,0)$ with the tagged preparation $B_A:=B\oplus I_{\mathbb C^n\otimes W}$. Implement its $B$ block with the supplied tag-controlled form of $B$ and charge that controlled preparation cost. The QLSP promise $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)$ removes the kernel component, and the output is tagged in the domain summand. All parameter comparisons, reversible arithmetic and finite-precision synthesis use the separately charged routines in the access model. The algorithm is the finite OP5 program:

1. Apply the supplied $B$ (or $B_A$ for a rectangular system) to prepare the input and its fixed work state, set $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, choose the least power of two $T\ge8(t_0+1)$ by certified comparisons, and let $L=\log_2T$. Initialize the phase register to $|0^L\rangle$ in big-endian order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$. This carrier chooses OP5's explicit table variant for preparing [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]]. Build the complete binary prefix tree on the $T$ leaves. At each level $\ell=0,\ldots,L-1$ and for each interval node $[a,b)$ at that level, put $m=(a+b)/2$ and compute the child masses $W_T(a,m)$ and $W_T(m,b)$ from the formula in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Store $r=W_T(a,m)/W_T(a,b)$ and apply $R_y(2\arcsin\sqrt r)$ to wire $q_{L-1-\ell}$, controlled on the preceding $\ell$ wires matching the path to $[a,b)$; encode bit $1$ as the left child and bit $0$ as the right child. The root has no controls. Thus the ideal circuit prepares $|\Psi_T\rangle$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]]. Put $\epsilon_\Psi=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. Each nonempty mass is at least $T^{-2}$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Use certified interval arithmetic with absolute mass error at most $\epsilon_\Psi^2/(10^6L^2T^4)$; refine until each stored angle and its finite gate synthesis together give controlled-rotation operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi/(100T)$. The cases $r=0$ and $r=1$ use the identity and $\pi$ rotations, respectively. Store each other angle with at least $\lceil\log_2(100\pi T/\epsilon_\Psi)\rceil+2$ bits. There are $T-1$ rotations; [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]] bounds their total operator error by $\epsilon_\Psi/100$ from the displayed combined per-node operator tolerance. The table contains $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations. Charge its one-time construction/data cost $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ and each forward/inverse preparation cost $C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ from [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]], including reversible lookup, control and finite gate synthesis. Thus the sine-preparation unitary and its inverse each have operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi$; this variant pays linear-in-$T$ table and rotation resources rather than assuming a loaded amplitude table.

2. In either the original full-space or alternative clean-workspace simulation mode, initialize all simulator work in zero and retain it coherently. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, set $t_j=2^jt_0/T$ and allocate $\eta_j=\epsilon/(8192\kappa L)$ to both its forward controlled call $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ and its reverse call. Apply $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ to the system controlled on wire $q_j$ being $1$, and act as identity on its $0$ branch. In the declared order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$, a phase label $\tau$ has bits $x_j$ with $\tau=\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}2^jx_j$, so the ideal controlled list applies $e^{+iH\tau t_0/T}$. Apply the negative-sign QFT, decode $y$ to signed $k=y$ for $y<T/2$ and $k=y-T$ otherwise, and set $\widetilde\lambda=2\pi k/t_0$. The total forward evolution time is $\sum_{j<L}t_j=t_0(1-1/T)<t_0$, and the sum of the $2L$ simulation error allocations is $\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. This uses the signed convention in [[lem-qa-26-phase-to-eigenvalue-unwrapping]].

3. Reversibly compute the flag angles and sign from $\widetilde\lambda$ using [[def-qa-26-hhl-reciprocal-filter]]. Use the two-qubit computational basis $|q_1q_0\rangle$ with labels $|\mathrm{nothing}\rangle=|00\rangle$, $|\mathrm{well}\rangle=|01\rangle$, $|\mathrm{ill}\rangle=|10\rangle$, and unused label $|11\rangle$. Write $p=|f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|$, $r=\sqrt{1-p^2}$, $\alpha=2\arcsin p$, and $\beta=2\arcsin(g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)/r)$. These are defined at every decoded grid point because [[lem-qa-26-hhl-filter-geometry]] gives $p\le1/2$, $0\le g\le1/2$, and $r\ge\sqrt3/2$, so $g/r\le1/\sqrt3<1$. First apply $R_y(\alpha)$ to $q_0$ conditioned on $q_1=0$, acting as identity on the $q_1=1$ subspace. Next apply $R_y(\beta)$ to $q_1$ conditioned on $q_0=0$, acting as identity on the $q_0=1$ subspace. Here $R_y(\theta)=\exp(-i\theta Y/2)$ with the exact convention and unitary formula of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and [[thm-qc-axis-rotation-pauli-formula]]. Finally apply $D_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,s,1,1)$ in the ordered flag basis, where $s=-1$ if $\widetilde\lambda<0$ and $s=+1$ otherwise (in particular at zero, where $f_\kappa(0)=0$). The resulting full flag unitary is $D_sG_{02}(\beta)G_{01}(\alpha)$: the two conditional rotations act as $R_y$ on the indicated two-label subspaces and as identity on their orthogonal complements, and $D_s$ is diagonal unitary. All three factors fix the unused label $|11\rangle$. On $|00\rangle$ the product gives $h(\widetilde\lambda)|00\rangle+f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|01\rangle+g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|10\rangle$, since $\cos(\beta/2)=h/r$ and $\sin(\beta/2)=g/r$. Uncompute the arithmetic. Synthesize the phase-controlled map with uniform operator error at most $\eta_R:=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$, charged through $C_{\rm flag}$ and $C_{\rm arith}$.

4. Reverse the QFT, every actual controlled simulation circuit, and sine preparation, retaining the flag and all simulator work. In clean-workspace mode the ideal trajectory has this work in zero; [[lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid]] bounds the complete attempt on that ideal trajectory without assuming actual intermediate work is clean. This gives a unitary flagged preparation $V$ and its exact circuit inverse $V^\dagger$. Let $\Pi_{\rm good}$ be the well-flag projection in Hermitian mode and the product of the well-flag projection and tagged domain projection in rectangular mode; these two projections act on distinct registers and commute. Let $p=\|\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle\|^2$. Apply the finite capped amplification procedure proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-capped-amplification]] with success projection $\Pi_{\rm good}$, lower bound $p_{\mathrm{low}}=1/(16\kappa^2)$ and failure target $\rho$. Its success reflection and verification test both the well flag and the domain tag in rectangular mode; charge their actual costs to $C_{\rm ref}$ and $C_{\rm ver}$. Measure $\{\Pi_{\rm good},I-\Pi_{\rm good}\}$ and return the conditional state, tagged output and success bit on success; return FAIL otherwise.

The circuit uses no uniform-register phase-tail estimate: its phase distribution is the sine-window kernel proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-kernel-moment]]. Its $G_\Psi,C_\Psi,C_{\rm sim},C_{\rm QFT}^{+/-},C_{\rm flag}$, reflection, verification and $B/B^\dagger$ costs remain separate inputs.

Let $L=\log_2T$, $t_j=2^jt_0/T$, $K=\lceil4\kappa\rceil$, and $R=\lceil16\ln(1/\rho)\rceil+16$. The capped HHL circuit uses at most $RK$ calls to each of $V$ and $V^\dagger$, at most $RK$ calls to each supplied preparation form (the tagged $B_A$ in dilation mode) and its inverse, and one table construction $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$. Each $V$ or $V^\dagger$ contains two sine-table preparation/unpreparation circuits, one forward and one inverse QFT, the flag circuit, and $2L$ controlled simulation calls at signed times $\pm t_j$; its absolute evolution times sum to less than $2t_0$. Therefore the total absolute simulation time is less than $4RKt_0=O(\kappa^2\epsilon^{-1}(1+\log(1/\rho)))$. More precisely, the simulation charge is the actual sum over all $V,V^\dagger$ calls of $\sum_{j<L}(C_{\rm sim}(t_j,\eta_j)+C_{\rm sim}(-t_j,\eta_j))$. The remaining charge is
$$G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)+n_VC_B+n_{V^\dagger}C_{B^\dagger}+2(n_V+n_{V^\dagger})C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)+(n_V+n_{V^\dagger})(C_{\rm QFT}^{+}(T)+C_{\rm QFT}^{-}(T)+C_{\rm flag}(\kappa,\eta_R)+C_{\rm arith}(T,\kappa,\epsilon))+N_{\rm ref}C_{\rm ref}+N_{\rm ver}C_{\rm ver},$$
where $n_V,n_{V^\dagger}\le RK$ and $N_{\rm ref},N_{\rm ver}$ are the actual reflection and verification counts. The table itself has $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ data bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations; no polylogarithmic table-generation or finite-rotation synthesis bound is asserted.

Under the promises and precision allocations in [[alg-qa-26-hhl-phase-estimation]], let $u=\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle$ be the actual joint success vector for one prepared attempt, where rectangular-mode success includes the domain-tag projection. Write $v_{\rm sys}=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$ and $v=v_{\rm sys}\otimes|g_B\rangle\otimes|0_{\rm alg}\rangle\otimes|\mathrm{well}\rangle$ for the ideal joint vector, including the unchanged preparation work and clean algorithmic registers. For $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $0<\rho<1$, the conditional returned joint pure-state ray (including unchanged preparation work) has a unit representative within vector norm $\epsilon$ of the normalized QLSP target tensored with the preparation work, clean algorithmic registers and well flag, and the capped amplification returns FAIL with probability at most $\rho$. The same assertion holds for the Hermitian dilation, with the output in its tagged domain summand.

Let $H$ be a self-adjoint endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex
inner-product space $V$. For real $t,s$, the evolution from
[[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]] satisfies
$$U_H(0)=I_V,\qquad U_H(t)^*U_H(t)=I_V,\qquad U_H(t+s)=U_H(t)U_H(s),\qquad \frac{d}{dt}U_H(t)=-iHU_H(t).$$
Moreover, $U_H$ is the unique differentiable map $Y:\mathbb R\to
\operatorname{End}(V)$ satisfying $Y'(t)=-iHY(t)$ and $Y(0)=I_V$.

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

Let $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ be a finite-dimensional linear map, $m,n\ge1$, and let $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)\setminus\{0\}$, where $\operatorname{ran}(A)$ is the image defined in [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **quantum linear-systems state-output task (QLSP)** is to prepare the normalized domain-register state
$$|x\rangle:=\frac{A^+b}{\|A^+b\|}\in\mathbb C^n,$$
where $A^+$ is the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. By [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]], write $b=\sum_{j:\sigma_j>0}\beta_j u_j$ in left singular vectors; the promised support gap is a supplied rational or exactly represented $\gamma>0$ such that every $j$ with $\beta_j\ne0$ has singular value $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$. The input includes a costed unitary $B$ mapping its designated all-zero input to $|b/\|b\|\rangle$ in the codomain register, tensored with a fixed work state. Its inverse, controlled access, and resource coordinates are specified in the separate HHL access model. If $b$ is multiplied by $c\ne0$, the normalized representative is multiplied by $c/|c|$, so its pure-state ray is unchanged. The task returns a quantum state (and may return a success flag); it does not promise a classical list of coordinates.

derivations.claim: For each $x$, the ratios $(b_x)_j/(b_x)_1=c_j/a$ are $1$ or $4$ when $a=1$, and $1/2$ or $2$ when $a=2$. Since $N\ge2$, at least one ratio determines $a$; each ratio then determines its corresponding $c_j$. Thus the $2^N$ inputs give $2^N$ distinct solution rays, with no ambiguity from a global phase.

Let $z$ be a classical coordinate output for one of these rays, phase-fixed so that its first coordinate is positive real. If $|z_j-(b_x)_j|<\delta:=1/(100\sqrt N)$ for every $j$, then $(b_x)_1\ge1/(4\sqrt N)$ because $a\ge1$ and $\|a e_1+\sum_{j\ge2}c_je_j\|\le4\sqrt N$. Hence $|z_1|\ge6/(25\sqrt N)$. For each $j\ge2$, $$\left|\frac{z_j}{z_1}-\frac{(b_x)_j}{(b_x)_1}\right|\le\frac{\delta}{|z_1|}\left(1+\frac{(b_x)_j}{(b_x)_1}\right)\le\frac5{24}<\frac14.$$ The four candidate ratios have pairwise separation at least $1/2$, so nearest-ratio decoding recovers $a$ and every $c_j$, hence all $N$ bits. Any unambiguous classical output code for all these rays therefore needs at least $2^N$ codewords and at least $N$ bits. This output-length requirement is independent of the ability to prepare or measure the corresponding quantum state.
